ghs.assessment: お嬢様 is left untranslated as 'ojou-sama,' and the English dialogue is missing its closing quotation mark.
ghs.remedy: Use an English address such as 'young lady' and close the quotation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Hey! Melancholic ojou-sama!

ghs.en: Touko: "What's with you all of today!"
ghs.assessment: さっきから means 'for a while now' or 'all this time.' 'All of today' expands the duration to the whole day.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What has been with you for a while now?!'

highlights.text: Touko: "What's with you all of today!"

rows.jp: 「食欲がなくても、体にはエサを与えておいた方がいい」
rows.en: “Even if you have no appetite, you should still feed your body.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even if there is no hunger, it is most appropriate to confer nourishment to the body."

rows.jp: 「精神より先に体が根を上げる」
rows.en: “Your body will give out before your mind does.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The roots of the body are easier to extirpate than the mind's."
ghs.assessment: 体が音を上げる means the body will give out or cry uncle before the mind does. The English invents bodily roots being extirpated and loses the mind-body endurance contrast.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Your body will give out before your mind does.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "The roots of the body are easier to extirpate than the mind's."

ghs.en: Touko: "Keep your big words of help!"
ghs.assessment: 大きなお世話 is the rebuff 'None of your business' or 'I don't need your concern.' 'Keep your big words of help' literalizes the components into a different and unidiomatic complaint.
ghs.remedy: Use 'None of your business!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Keep your big words of help!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "You're good at cooking, if I remember."

rows.jp: 顔を向けようともしない。
rows.en: She wouldn’t even look at me.

ghs.en: She doesn't want to turn this way.
Taichi: "Just no helping you, is there."
Taichi: "Come on, out with that hand."

rows.jp: 冬子の顔に、刑事ばりに疑惑が満ちた。
rows.en: Touko’s face filled with detective-grade suspicion.

ghs.en: A suspicion reminiscent of a detective's filled Touko's face.

rows.jp: 本物の刑事は疑っても表情には出さないだろうが。
rows.en: Though a real detective would know better than to show it.

ghs.en: But a real detective, even if suspicious, wouldn't show that on his face.

rows.jp: 「……またヘンなもの握らせるつもりでしょ」
rows.en: “...You’re going to make me hold something weird again, aren’t you?”

ghs.en: Touko: "...you just want me to grab something weird again."

rows.jp: 「ヘッ、前にそんなことをしたことがあるみたいな言いぐさだな」
rows.en: “Hah! The way you say that, you’d think I’d ever done something like that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eeeh, you phrased that remark as if there was another event in the past similar to what you describe."

rows.jp: ペッ、と架空の唾を吐く（社会性）。
rows.en: Ptooey. I spat an imaginary loogie. (Social graces.)

ghs.assessment: Politeness compresses 社会性 inside the joke. The lexical narrowing and grammar are minor, not a moderate semantic failure.
ghs.remedy: Use social skills or sociability if the broader sense matters.

highlights.text: Pah!, I Imaginarily expectorated (politeness).

ghs.assessment: したじゃないのさ is Tōko's direct accusation: 'You did!' 'Wasn't there now' removes the actor and turns the remembered act into the existence of an event.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You did do it!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Wasn't there now!"

rows.jp: 「したじゃないのしたじゃないのっ、ぎゅっとぎゅーっと握らせたじゃないのっ」
rows.en: “You did! You did! You made me hold it—made me squeeze it tight!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Wasn't there now, wasn't there now, all squeeze-squeeezing what you put in my hand, wasn't there!"
ghs.assessment: Tōko repeats that he did it and made her grip the object tightly. The English is syntactically incoherent and turns 'made me grip' into an unidentified thing he put in her hand.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You did, you did! You made me squeeze it—really squeeze it!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Wasn't there now, wasn't there now, all squeeze-squeeezing what you put in my hand, wasn't there!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "There were such things as those?"
ghs.assessment: そんなこと is number-neutral, so number alone cannot sustain the finding. The confirmed issue is grammar and how the recollection is framed.
ghs.remedy: Render the recollection naturally without forcing number.

highlights.text: Taichi: "There were such things as those?"

rows.jp: アホの子供みたいな口調で言う。
rows.en: I said it in the voice of an especially stupid child.

ghs.en: I used an expression as that of a dumb child.
ghs.assessment: 口調 means tone or manner of speaking. 'Used an expression' instead suggests a facial expression and fails to identify the childlike voice.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I say it in the tone of a stupid child.'

highlights.text: I used an expression as that of a dumb child.

rows.jp: 「うそ！　その顔は絶対おぼえてる顔！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Lies! That face is the face of someone who absolutely remembers!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Tōko as the speaker accusing the narrator of remembering. The English labels the line as Taichi, making him accuse his own face.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to Tōko.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Lies! That face is the face of someone who absolutely remembers!"

rows.jp: 「こっちはまだ感触が手に残ってるのに～っ！」
rows.en: “I can still feel it in my hand!”

ghs.en: Touko: "The feeling of that thing still remains on my haaa～nd!"
She shaked and trembled with fear.
ghs.assessment: Fear is unsupported against the contextually clear rage, but the broken form shaked is also central. Critical severity overstates the damage.
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical expression of rage.

highlights.text: She shaked and trembled with fear.

rows.jp: 「だいたいアンタ！　人の頭の上に乗っけたこともあったでしょ！」
rows.en: “And you! You put it on top of my head, too!”

ghs.en: Touko: "By the way, you! There's also how you put that thing over people's heads wasn't there!"
ghs.assessment: 人の頭 is a generic or indirect way to mean someone's or my head. The remaining defect is grammar and preposition, not number.
ghs.remedy: Render the indirect head reference naturally.

highlights.text: Touko: "By the way, you! There's also how you put that thing over people's heads wasn't there!"

rows.jp: 禁断の秘技、ちょんまげ。
rows.en: The forbidden secret technique: the Cockknot.

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's common in the mannerisms of aristocrats!"
ghs.assessment: たしなみ here is a cultivated accomplishment or customary practice, not 'common in the mannerisms.' The English also pluralizes the term and adds frequency.
ghs.remedy: Use 'An aristocratic accomplishment.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's common in the mannerisms of aristocrats!"

rows.jp: 「性犯罪者のたしなみでしょ！！　貴族があんなことするかぁっ！！」
rows.en: “A sex offender’s refinement! What nobleman would ever do that?!”

ghs.en: Touko: "That's the mannerism of a sex offender!!! Whyyy would an aristocrat do that!!!"
Taichi: "Because she's more than a bit perverted, that's why."
ghs.assessment: 自分だってエロいくせに accuses the addressee directly: 'You're perverted too.' The English changes the subject to a third-person woman and makes her perversion the reason for the prior aristocrat claim.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As if you aren't perverted yourself.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because she's more than a bit perverted, that's why."

rows.jp: 蒼白だった顔がもっとまっしろに。
rows.en: Her already bloodless face went dead white.

ghs.en: Her already pale face went even whiter.

ghs.assessment: The callback supports one finger, though Japanese morphology alone need not mark number. Treat this as a context-sensitive callback issue.
ghs.remedy: Match the established singular-finger callback.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Now, using my fingers---"

rows.jp: 「おのれがやらせたんじゃーーーーーーーーーっっ！」
rows.en: “YOU’RE THE ONE WHO MADE ME DO IIIIIIIIIIIIT!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Didn't you make me DO THAT YOU BAAAAAAAAASTARD!!!"

ghs.assessment: GHS replaces the source's exact English I am the winner with a different recognizable broken-English victory meme. The function survives, but the allusion is substituted.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the source's exact English victory line.

highlights.text: Taichi: "CONGRATURATION YOU ARE WINNER."

ghs.en: I fluttered and twisted in the air.
ghs.assessment: 舞った can mean danced or fluttered, so GHS's motion is possible. The difference is motion and intensity, not categorical failure.
ghs.remedy: Use a context-appropriate airborne motion.

highlights.text: I fluttered and twisted in the air.

rows.jp: 放物線を描いて落ちた。
rows.en: I came down in a perfect arc.

ghs.en: I fell while delineating a parabola.

rows.jp: 「これが我が魂的責務とはいえ……いたい……いたいよ……」
rows.en: “It may be my soul’s solemn duty, but... ow... owww...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "This may be an obligation written in Our soul, but... owww... that hurt..."
ghs.assessment: 我が is archaic my. GHS's plural is a real but small number-and-voice shift.
ghs.remedy: Keep the archaic singular possessive.

highlights.text: Taichi: "This may be an obligation written in Our soul, but... owww... that hurt..."

rows.jp: 起きて、のたくたと散乱した机と椅子を並べ直す。
rows.en: I hauled myself up, writhing, and put the scattered desks and chairs back in place.

ghs.en: Getting up, I sluggishly rearrange the chairs and desks that were scattered.

rows.jp: 冬子はもう元の姿勢に戻っていた。
rows.en: Touko was already back in her original pose.

ghs.en: Touko had already returned in her original posture.
ghs.assessment: 戻る takes the destination particle に in Japanese, but English returns 'to' a posture rather than 'in' it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko had already returned to her original posture.'

highlights.text: Touko had already returned in her original posture.

rows.jp: 形状記憶合金なみの体面だった。
rows.en: Her dignity snapped back into place like shape-memory alloy.

ghs.en: Her entire persona is like a shape memory alloy.
ghs.assessment: 体面 is her composure, dignity, or outward front, likened to shape-memory alloy for snapping back into form. 'Entire persona' replaces that recoverable social surface with her whole personality.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her composure had the resilience of shape-memory alloy.'

highlights.text: Her entire persona is like a shape memory alloy.

rows.jp: 「はいはい、無視なら無視でいいけどさ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Fine, fine, if you gotta ignore you'll just ignore."
ghs.assessment: The source concedes that being ignored is fine if that is her choice. 'If you gotta ignore you'll just ignore' is a tautological conditional with no grammatical object.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Fine, fine. Ignore me if you want.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Fine, fine, if you gotta ignore you'll just ignore."

ghs.assessment: ちょっと is a protest such as 'Wait' or 'Hey.' 'Really' instead expresses disbelief or emphasis and does not object to the immediate action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wait...'

highlights.text: Touko: "Really..."

ghs.assessment: ぽたぽた represents several small objects dropping one after another. 'Pik pik pik' is an unexplained invented sound that suggests sharp electronic beeps.
ghs.remedy: Use a legible dropping sound or project the three small impacts typographically.

highlights.text: Pik pik pik.

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's like your mommy used to make."
ghs.assessment: ママの味 is the candy slogan 'the taste of mama,' and くらえ is an aggressive command to receive or taste it. 'It's like your mommy used to make' converts it into her personal childhood food and removes the command.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Taste the flavor of mama.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's like your mommy used to make."

rows.jp: てのひらに転がる、あめ玉みっつ。
rows.en: Three hard candies rolled into her palm.

ghs.en: In her palm rolled candies three.
ghs.assessment: The source presents three pieces of candy rolling into or across her palm. 'In her palm rolled candies three' uses broken inversion and archaic postposed counting.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Three pieces of candy roll into her palm.'

highlights.text: In her palm rolled candies three.

rows.jp: 「安心するがいい。俺の二億匹の小さなワンダフルライフたちは入ってないから」
rows.en: “Rest easy. My two hundred million little wonderful lives aren’t in there.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You can be at ease. My two hundred million little wonderful lives aren't inside."

ghs.assessment: The source says they are on vacation, followed by the marked parenthetical 米笑. 'Furlough' changes an ordinary vacation to authorized leave, and 'ULOL' is an unexplained invented initialism.
ghs.remedy: Use 'They're on vacation' and preserve or transparently gloss the marked laughter notation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "They're on furlough! (ULOL)"

ghs.assessment: 当たり前でしょ means 'Of course' or 'Obviously.' 'So typical' instead judges the preceding conduct as habitual.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Obviously.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...so typical."

rows.jp: 冬子はあめ玉を握った。
rows.en: Touko closed her hand around the candies.

rows.jp: 「糖分を等分に摂取すれば当分は生きられるはずだ」
rows.en: “A fair share of sugar will keep you in fair shape for a fair while.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If your sugar level levels level should your life expectancy too."

rows.jp: ダジャレも三重なら許されるはずだった。
rows.en: Three fairs ought to make the pun legal.

ghs.en: And that triple-use joke should also be forgiven.

rows.jp: 「食欲がなくとも、ものを口に入れる習慣は維持するように」
rows.en: “Even if you’re not hungry, keep up the habit of putting something in your mouth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even if hunger is missing, it is important to make a habit of putting things in the mouth."
ghs.assessment: 食欲がなくとも means even without an appetite, not that hunger itself is 'missing.' 'Putting things in the mouth' is also a literal bodily description where English says to keep eating.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even if you have no appetite, keep up the habit of eating.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Even if hunger is missing, it is important to make a habit of putting things in the mouth."

rows.jp: 冬子はじっと拳を見つめていた。
rows.en: Touko stared at her closed fist.

ghs.en: Touko gazed, fixedly, at her fist.

rows.jp: 「優しいフリをしたり、バカにしたり、冷たくしたり、恐くなったり」
rows.en: “You pretend to be kind, make fun of me, turn cold, scare me...”

ghs.en: Touko: "Pretending to be nice, acting the fool, becoming cold and distant, getting scary."
ghs.assessment: バカにしたり means making fun of or belittling the speaker. 'Acting the fool' instead makes the addressee behave foolishly and removes the interpersonal target.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Pretending to be kind, making fun of me, turning cold, becoming frightening...'

highlights.text: Touko: "Pretending to be nice, acting the fool, becoming cold and distant, getting scary."

ghs.en: Touko: "...leave me alone. I'm begging you."

ghs.assessment: 怒られた means the narrator was scolded. 'She was angered' makes Tōko the passive experiencer of anger and omits the act directed at him.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She scolded me.' or 'I got told off.'

highlights.text: She was angered.
